skills.description: Ask which skill or flow fits your situation. A router over the skills in this repo.
skills.reason: The existing Harness and Skill routing already choose applicable AIPS Skills; a second router would duplicate selection.

skills.description: Review the changes since a fixed point (commit, branch, tag, or merge-base) along two axes: Standards (does the code follow this repo's documented coding standards?) and Spec (does the code match what the originating issue/spec asked for?). Runs both reviews in parallel sub-agents and reports them side by side. Use when the user wants to review a branch, a PR, work-in-progress changes, or asks to "review since X".
skills.reason: Adds separate Standards and Spec lenses, a fixed comparison point and evidence-backed findings.

skills.description: Shared vocabulary for designing deep modules. Use when the user wants to design or improve a module's interface, find deepening opportunities, decide where a seam goes, make code more testable or AI-navigable, or when another skill needs the deep-module vocabulary.
skills.reason: Adds deep-module, seam and interface vocabulary to the existing architecture Skill.

skills.description: Diagnosis loop for hard bugs and performance regressions. Use when the user says "diagnose"/"debug this", or reports something broken/throwing/failing/slow.
skills.reason: Adds a tight failing loop, minimization and falsifiable hypotheses to the existing debugging method.

skills.description: Build and sharpen a project's domain model. Use when discussing codebase terminology, writing or editing a GLOSSARY.md, or recording or editing an ADR.
skills.reason: Adds glossary terminology checks and example-based model validation without duplicating DDD or ADR Skills.

skills.description: A relentless interview to sharpen a plan or design, which also creates docs (ADR's and glossary) as we go.
skills.reason: AIPS already has requirement clarification and project knowledge mechanisms; preserve the outputs without a second interview skill.

skills.description: Implement a piece of work based on a spec or set of tickets.
skills.reason: The existing implementation, TDD and review flow already covers the responsibility.

skills.description: Implement the result of /to-spec and /to-tickets in code.
skills.reason: Integrate task dependency mapping into the existing planning and scheduling flow.

skills.description: Scan a codebase for deepening opportunities, present them as a visual HTML report, then grill through whichever one you pick.
skills.reason: Adds architecture improvement candidates and deep-module checks to the existing architecture Skill.

skills.description: Use when writing a PR body.
skills.reason: AIPS has a governed Git publication proposal and Human merge authority.

skills.description: Build a throwaway prototype to answer a design question. Use when the user wants to sanity-check whether a state model or logic feels right, or explore what a UI should look like.
skills.reason: Distinct throwaway prototype discipline; isolated from production code and runtime credentials.

skills.description: Investigate a question against high-trust primary sources and capture the findings as a Markdown file in the repo. Use when the user wants a topic researched, docs or API facts gathered, or reading legwork delegated to a background agent.
skills.reason: Distinct technical primary-source research; product and market evidence stays in product-research.

skills.description: Conduct a retrospective on a coding session.
skills.reason: Existing self-improvement review proposes evidence-based system changes and does not silently modify core policy.

skills.description: Configure this repo for the engineering skills: set up its issue tracker, triage label vocabulary, and domain doc layout. Run once before first use of the other engineering skills.
skills.reason: Upstream-specific installation and tracker setup would create a second Skill system and could bypass AIPS ownership.

skills.description: Test-driven development. Use when the user wants to build features or fix bugs test-first, mentions "red-green-refactor", or wants integration tests.
skills.reason: Adds public-seam, independent-expectation and vertical-slice test quality rules.

skills.description: Turn the current conversation into a spec and publish it to the project issue tracker: no interview, just synthesis of what you've already discussed.
skills.reason: The existing requirement workflow turns accepted user intent into a traceable specification.

skills.description: Break a plan, spec, or the current conversation into a set of tracer-bullet tickets, each declaring its blocking edges, published to the configured tracker (edges as text in one file per ticket locally, or native blocking links on a real tracker).
skills.reason: Adds vertical slices, dependency edges, verification and traceability.

skills.description: Move issues and external PRs through a state machine of triage roles, categorise, verify, grill if needed, and write agent-ready briefs.
skills.reason: Distinct evidence-led issue classification; tracker writes remain explicitly authorized.

skills.description: Plan a huge chunk of work (more than one agent session can hold) as a shared map of decision tickets on your issue tracker, and resolve them one at a time until the way to the destination is clear.
skills.reason: The existing planning package and scheduler cover long-running dependency maps.

skills.description: Generate an interactive bash wizard that walks a human through steps only they can perform. Use when provisioning infrastructure, setting up credentials or CI secrets, walking an unfamiliar third-party dashboard, or running a one-off migration or cutover. Don't invoke this for steps the agent can perform itself.
skills.reason: Distinct human-only external steps; no secret collection or privileged execution.

skills.description: Pursue a long-running goal in a single session by co-ordinating subagents.
skills.reason: Do not test the Beta orchestration model or grant autonomous long-running authority.

skills.description: Hand the current conversation off to a fresh background agent that picks up the work immediately.
skills.reason: Keep AIPS checkpoint and Host-specific handoff boundaries.

skills.description: Grill me about specs for the workflows I want to build, within this workspace.
skills.reason: The user explicitly excluded other Beta Skill trials.

skills.description: Wire dependency-cruiser into a TypeScript repo so each package is a deep module, with implementation hidden in subfolders and reachable only through its entry-point files. User-invoked.
skills.reason: Preserve as upstream technical reference; no TypeScript Beta trial or project mutation.

skills.description: Writing, exploit; assemble raw material into a journey of beats, grounding each term before a beat leans on it.
skills.reason: User explicitly selected the optional Writing workflow; invoke only on explicit request.

skills.description: Writing, explore: mine raw fragments, no structure yet.
skills.reason: User explicitly selected the optional Writing workflow; invoke only on explicit request.

skills.description: Writing, exploit: shape raw material into an article, paragraph by paragraph.
skills.reason: User explicitly selected the optional Writing workflow; invoke only on explicit request.

skills.description: Set up Claude Code hooks to block dangerous git commands (push, reset --hard, clean, branch -D, etc.) before they execute. Use when user wants to prevent destructive git operations, add git safety hooks, or block git push/reset in Claude Code.
skills.reason: AIPS already owns cross-runtime Git publication guardrails and Human authority.

skills.description: Migrate test files from `as` type assertions to @total-typescript/shoehorn. Use when user mentions shoehorn, wants to replace `as` in tests, or needs partial test data.
skills.reason: Framework-specific migration belongs in a TypeScript project when requested.

skills.description: Create exercise directory structures with sections, problems, solutions, and explainers that pass linting. Use when user wants to scaffold exercises, create exercise stubs, or set up a new course section.
skills.reason: Course scaffolding is project-specific; the reusable teaching method is captured separately.

skills.description: Set up Husky pre-commit hooks with lint-staged (Prettier), type checking, and tests in the current repo. Use when user wants to add pre-commit hooks, set up Husky, configure lint-staged, or add commit-time formatting/typechecking/testing.
skills.reason: Hook choice is project-specific and may conflict with existing tooling.

skills.description: A relentless interview to sharpen a plan or design.
skills.reason: User-invoked clarification already has a governed AIPS path.

skills.description: Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases.
skills.reason: Shared clarification method belongs in one AIPS requirements workflow.

skills.description: Compact the current conversation into a handoff document for another agent to pick up.
skills.reason: AIPS already has checkpoint and task handoff conventions.

skills.description: Teach the user a new skill or concept, within this workspace.
skills.reason: Adds a distinct goal-practice-feedback teaching loop.

skills.description: Turn a decision you can't fully answer into a questionnaire for someone else to fill in.
skills.reason: Questionnaire output is a format extension to requirement clarification.

skills.description: Stop. That last message did not land: re-pitch it.
skills.reason: Plain-language explanations are already part of the Human communication contract.

skills.description: Writing documents for agents. Use when creating or editing skills, or modifying AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md.
skills.reason: Existing admission and documentation rules own reusable agent writing guidance.
